rationale.intervention_reconstruction: The hypothesis proposes thermal aging at 700–900°C to induce grain boundary segregation, while the target uses aging at ~600°C and ~750°C to manipulate L12 ordering and phase boundary morphology. Both involve thermal aging, but the specific temperature windows and the underlying lever (segregation vs. ordering) differ.
rationale.condition_agreement: The hypothesis uses aging at 700–900°C in inert atmosphere with subsequent mechanical testing at ambient and low temperatures, whereas the target focuses on a 550–750°C window with ductility measured at room temperature. The temperature regimes overlap only partially, and the testing conditions differ in specifics.
rationale.mechanism_agreement: The hypothesis invokes nanoscale grain boundary segregation reducing interfacial cohesion, while the target mechanism involves enhanced L12 ordering restricting cross-slip and stress concentration at jagged phase boundaries. These are different classes of embrittlement mechanisms.
rationale.outcome_agreement: The hypothesis predicts a monotonic toughness decrease after aging, while the target predicts a non-monotonic ductile-brittle-ductile transition with minimum ductility at 600°C and recovery at 750°C. The predicted property (toughness/ductility) and direction (decrease) agree only in part, but the overall pattern differs.
